mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative despite sustained FEDFUNDS > 4% for 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coincides with stronger consumer demand (GDPC1), amplifying corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate exceeds 200,000 for two consecutive months and GDPC1 > 2% MoM
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon when both proxies show strong growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month average followed by a rebound suggests cyclical bottoming, which precedes a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month avg and INDPRO crosses above 12-month avg in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative for 5 consecutive such cycles.

mechanism_narrative: When supply-side pressures (RSAFS) rise while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2%, it indicates a tight supply environment that supports higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% and RSAFS > 250M for two consecutive months
regime_hint: suppressed inflation with rising supply pressures
failure_condition: Walk-forward IC > 0.1 over the 20-day horizon in such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% without a corresponding rise in inflation triggers a Fed easing cycle that boosts equity valuations, producing positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 4 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 0.5% over the same period
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE remaining < 4% for 12 months.

failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) lags for two consecutive months followed by a sharp rebound, it signals a supply-side release that supports higher equity valuations and positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving avg for 2 months and then crosses above in the third month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative during such recoveries.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the 10-year yield (not available) — instead: A sustained rise in FEDFUNDS above 5% for 6 months is associated with a sharp decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to compressed discounting.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative during such periods.
